segments.text: Lesson 35
segments.translation: 第35课

segments.text: Space odyssey
segments.translation: 太空漫游

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: When will it be possible for us to think seriously about colonising Mars?
segments.translation: 我们什么时候才能认真考虑殖民火星？

segments.text: The Moon is likely to become the industrial hub of the Solar System supplying the rocket fuels for its ships,
segments.translation: 月球很可能成为太阳系的工业中心，为其飞船提供火箭燃料，

segments.text: easily obtainable from the lunar rocks in the form of liquid oxygen.
segments.translation: 很容易从月球岩石中以液氧的形式获得。

segments.text: The reason lies in its gravity.
segments.translation: 原因就在于它的重力。

segments.text: Because the Moon has only an eightieth of the Earth's mass,
segments.translation: 因为月球的质量只有地球的八十分之一，

segments.text: it requires 97% less energy
segments.translation: 所需能源减少 97%

segments.text: to travel the quarter of a million miles from the Moon to Earth-orbit than the 200 mile-journey from Earth's surface into orbit!
segments.translation: 从月球到地球轨道行驶 25 万英里比从地球表面进入轨道 200 英里的旅程还要多！

segments.text: This may sound fantastic, but it is easily calculated.
segments.translation: 这听起来可能很不可思议，但很容易计算。

segments.text: To escape from the Earth in a rocket, one must travel at seven miles per second.
segments.translation: 要乘坐火箭逃离地球，必须以每秒七英里的速度行驶。

segments.text: The comparable speed from the Moon is only 1.5 miles per second.
segments.translation: 从月球出发的可比速度仅为每秒 1.5 英里。

segments.text: Because the gravity on the Moon's surface is only a sixth of Earth's (remember how easily the Apollo astronauts bounded along),
segments.translation: 因为月球表面的重力只有地球的六分之一（还记得阿波罗宇航员是多么轻松地跳跃），

segments.text: it takes much less energy to accelerate to that 1.5mps than it does on Earth.
segments.translation: 加速到 1.5mps 所需的能量比在地球上少得多。

segments.text: Moon dwellers will be able to fly in space at only three percent of the cost of similar journeys by their terrestrial cousins.
segments.translation: 月球居民将能够在太空中飞行，而成本仅为其陆地表亲类似旅程的百分之三。

segments.text: Arthur C.Clark once suggested a revolutionary idea passes through three phases:
segments.translation: 亚瑟·C·克拉克 (Arthur C.Clark) 曾经提出，一个革命性的想法要经历三个阶段：

segments.text: 1.  'It's impossible--don't waste my time.'
segments.translation: 1.“这是不可能的——别浪费我的时间。”

segments.text: 2.  'It's possible, but not worth doing.'
segments.translation: 2.“这是可能的，但不值得这样做。”

segments.text: 3.  'I said it was a good idea all along.'
segments.translation: 3.“我一直说这是个好主意。”

segments.text: The idea of colonising Mars--a world 160 times more distant than the Moon--will move decisively from the second phase to the third,
segments.translation: 殖民火星——一个比月球远160倍的世界——的想法将决定性地从第二阶段转向第三阶段，

segments.text: when a significant number of people are living permanently in space.
segments.translation: 当相当多的人永久生活在太空中时。

segments.text: Mars has an extraordinary fascination for would-be voyagers.
segments.translation: 火星对未来的航行者有着非凡的吸引力。

segments.text: America, Russia and Europe are filled with enthusiasts--many of them serious and senior scientists who dream of sending people to it.
segments.translation: 美国、俄罗斯和欧洲充满了狂热者——其中许多人都是严肃而资深的科学家，梦想着将人们送往那里。

segments.text: Their aim is understandable.
segments.translation: 他们的目的是可以理解的。

segments.text: It is the one world in the Solar System that is most like the Earth.
segments.translation: 它是太阳系中最像地球的一个世界。

segments.text: It is a world of red sandy deserts (hence its name--the Red Planet),
segments.translation: 这是一个红色沙漠的世界（因此得名——红色星球），

segments.text: cloudless skies, savage sandstorms, chasms wider than the Grand Canyon and at least one mountain more than twice as tall as Everest.
segments.translation: 万里无云的天空、狂暴的沙尘暴、比大峡谷还宽的峡谷，以及至少一座比珠穆朗玛峰高两倍以上的山峰。

segments.text: It seems ideal for settlement.
segments.translation: 这似乎是解决问题的理想选择。
